claims.claim: With a block-only receptive field (h = 0), closure and the local-law objective rediscover block mass on their own: the learned c = 1 latent and block mass predict each other with cross-validated R^2 >= 0.93 both ways, identically across seeds (seed R^2 >= 0.997).

Reconstruction with the nonlinear local encoder does not: at h = 0 it learns a seed-dependent feature that is not mass and is barely predictable (ceiling at h = 4 of 0.09 vs 0.77 for block mass); the linear (L) and the unconstrained (U) autoencoders at c = 1 do land on block mass (first principal component of block content).

With a halo the closure latent becomes a low-pass filtered mass field: it stays a function of block mass (R^2(Z | mass) 0.88-0.98) but block mass is no longer recoverable from it (R^2(mass | Z) falls 0.93 -> 0.61), it agrees best with the designed tent at h = 4-8 (R^2 0.93-0.97 both ways), its closure ceiling at h = 16 rises 0.16 -> 0.27 -> 0.38 -> 0.55 with halo 0, 4, 8, 16 px, while its effective dimension (participation ratio) falls 44 -> 13 and its predictable content (I_avail at h = 1) falls 214 -> 174 nats.

The hand designs keep the most predictable content per number: block mass I_avail / I_capt at h = 1 = 275 / 165 nats vs at most 266 / 163 for any learned c = 1 latent (L4_local; N arm best N0_local 246 / 146); block channel means (c = 2) 432 / 246 vs at most 404 (U_local) / 227 (N4_local) for learned c = 2 latents. Higher learned closure ceilings are bought by smoothing.

A shared local rule (local law) is at least as good a bias as the global closure head at every receptive field: higher captured predictive information at h = 1 and equal or higher ceilings, and closer to block mass.
Locality is what lets closure find mass: the unconstrained encoder trained for closure is less closed than block mass at every horizon, agrees with it poorly and is seed-unstable.
The predictive bottleneck lands in between: partly mass, less closed than block mass beyond h = 2.

Extra width (c = 2, 4) adds content that is less closed: the mass is still contained (R^2(mass | Z) >= 0.93 for N0 closure) but most of the latent is not mass, the second channel is not the per-channel block mass (R^2(Z | channel means) 0.51 for N0_clos_c2), and the h = 16 ceiling falls with width.
No bias at c <= 4 finds the object view: the best learned latent explains the object mass field no better than block mass does.

Closure-type latents are seed-stable and so are their ceilings (largest seed difference of the G ceiling over all c = 1 closure/local configs and horizons is 0.014); nonlinear reconstruction is not (seed R^2 0.08-0.87).
Cost of the study (billed): r4-bias-001 $0.81 (cancelled), r4-bias-002 $1.13 (cancelled), r4-bias-003 $6.01 (done); pod hours 0.396 + 0.447 + 1.951 = 2.79.
